content:
Hey everyone:) I wanted to introduce lev which is like uv but for lean because I kept wanting a faster, more consistent way to move between Lean projects, benchmark versions, and toolchains. Lean already has the important pieces: Elan for toolchains, Lake for projects and dependencies, and Mathlib caches for making large builds practical. But with the rise of LLMs and many people testing Lean systems across different benchmarks, versions, and repos, it becomes increasingly useful to have one predictable workflow layer for setup, syncing, caching, updating, and diagnosing project environments.

I also went through some zulip conversations, and this seems to be a recurring theme rather than just my own annoyance. Threads like lean, elan, leanpkg, leanproject -- documentation?, lean package manager, Running lake cache without updating the lean toolchain, Updating using lake again, and the many lake exe cache get discussions all point at the same rough edge: the Lean ecosystem has powerful tools, but the everyday workflow still asks users to know too many internal boundaries.

Lev is my attempt at a small uv-inspired layer over that workflow (I used codex to help a lot with the prototype and tested extensively for several months on many of my projects). It is not trying to replace Elan or Lake. Instead, it tries to make the common path clearer: create or enter a Lean project, pin the toolchain, sync dependencies, fetch caches, update deliberately, and diagnose what changed. I’m putting it out early because I’d like it to be useful to the community, and I’d especially welcome discussion about what the right interface should be and how to make it better or in the worst case these features already exist somewhere and I did not know of it:)!

Code: https://github.com/Robertboy18/lev
Blog post for more motivation: https://www.robertj1.com/ai4science/lev/
